body:
_Migrated from issue #1259, filed 2026-07-30._

Found in the cross-family review of #1258, which fixed the neighbouring case. Filing rather than widening that PR, because a complete fix restructures the publish sequence and #1258's change is narrow.

**What's covered now.** `scripts/publish-cwasync-plugin.sh` publishes the KOReader plugin to `new-usemame/cwasync.koplugin` and, as of #1258, attaches the same zip to the application release. If that application upload fails, a re-run now reconciles it: the plugin being unchanged plus a dedicated release existing for the tag means an earlier run got part-way, so the asset is copied down and attached. Pinned by `test_failed_application_upload_is_repaired_by_a_rerun`.

**What isn't.** The publish sequence is:

```
git push origin HEAD:main "$TAG"      # (1)
gh release create "$TAG" ...          # (2)
gh release upload "$TAG" ... (app)    # (3)  <- #1258 made a failure here recoverable
```

A failure between (1) and (2) leaves the dedicated repository's `main` and tag updated with **no release attached**. The owed-check reads `main`, so on the next run the plugin is byte-identical to what `main` ships and `publish_owed` is 0. The dedicated release does not exist, so the reconcile branch doesn't apply either, and the run takes the `Nothing owed … Skipping` exit and returns 0.

Result: the plugin is silently absent from the primary update channel — the one Updates Manager and appstore.koplugin actually read — and the workflow is green. This is worse than the case #1258 fixed, which only stranded devices still pointed at the application repository.

This is pre-existing and unchanged by #1258; the same window existed before that PR.

**Why the discriminator has to change.** "Nothing owed" currently means two different things and the check can't tell them apart. `main` matching the source means either this tag never touched the plugin (the common case) or a previous run pushed and then died. #1258 used *dedicated release exists* to split the second case out; the remaining case needs *dedicated tag pushed but no release*, e.g. `git ls-remote --exit-code --tags origin "refs/tags/$TAG"`.

**Why it isn't a one-liner.** Resuming from that state means creating the release (and then attaching the app asset) while skipping the commit/tag/push that already happened. Today those are straight-line statements, so the honest fix is to make each post-push step separately checked and separately resumable — "what does this tag still owe?" rather than "is a publish owed?". That's worth doing deliberately, with the fake-`gh`/`git` harness in `tests/unit/test_1253_plugin_release_asset_publish_paths.py` extended to cover each partial-failure point.

Also worth folding in: `gh release create` at (2) failing because the release already exists is currently a hard error at the guard above it, which is correct for a fresh publish and wrong for a resume.

No user has hit this. Filing it so a green workflow can't keep meaning "the plugin shipped" when it doesn't.
title: Plugin publish is only partly resumable: a push that lands with no release still reports success
